full_target:
Here dimension means **Hausdorff dimension**. As approved by the user on
2026-10-23, assume explicitly that \(E\) is nonempty. With the convention
\(\dim_H\varnothing=0\), the printed equality would otherwise fail for
the empty set. This is a disclosed addition to the printed exercise.

Let \(n\geq0\) be an integer, let \(E\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty
compact set, and put \(I=[0,1]\). Identify \(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\)
with \(\mathbb R^{n+1}\) and use its Euclidean metric. Prove

\[
\dim_H(E\times[0,1])=\dim_H E+1.
\]

The zero-dimensional ambient space \(\mathbb R^0\) is included. A later
formalization using a different product norm must justify the metric change.
proof:
We prove precisely the full selected target. Let n∈ℕ be arbitrary, including zero, and let E⊆ℝ^n be compact and nonempty, as stipulated in the input. There are no other hypotheses, and no algorithm is part of this target. Write X_n=EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), I=[0,1]⊆ℝ, and P=E×I⊆X_n×ℝ. Temporarily give X_n×ℝ its standard maximum metric. Let j_n(x,t)=(x_0,…,x_{n−1},t) in Euclidean X_{n+1}, and F=j_n(P). These are exactly join and cylinder in lean_header. In particular F, with its Euclidean metric, is the requested set under the specified coordinate identification; the maximum metric is only an intermediate representation. B010 is an already prepared Lean proof that dimH F=dimH P, with an explicit inverse deleting the last coordinate. It applies for every n, including zero.

The following derivations are the class-3 part of the basis. All sums of nonnegative costs and integrals are interpreted in [0,∞]; no convergence is presumed. For a finite real number a≥0 its embedding in this extended space is understood. Real powers at zero below are only used with a strictly positive exponent, so 0^s=0. Diameters are suprema of pairwise distances; empty sets have diameter zero. We freely use ordinary finite real/extended-nonnegative-real arithmetic and its complete order, and the pinned Mathlib's definitions and basic sum operations. The registered dependencies are mathematical grounds, not a restriction on later use of the rest of pinned Mathlib.

B101: Exact covering contents and scale conventions.
For any metric space X, A⊆X, real s>0 and r∈[0,∞], define C_s(r,A) to be the infimum over U:ℕ→Set X with A⊆⋃_i U_i and ediam U_i≤r for all i, of Σ_i(ediam U_i)^s. This is the object content in lean_header. An infimum over no admissible covers is ∞. For every particular admissible cover, the defining infimum is at most that cover's cost.

Give X its Borel measurable structure when writing μH[s]. B001 says μH[s](A) is the supremum over positive extended scales r of the same covering infima, with each cost written sup_{h:U_i.Nonempty}(ediam U_i)^s. If U_i is nonempty this supremum equals (ediam U_i)^s. If U_i is empty, ediam U_i=0 and both costs are zero because s>0. Thus
  μH[s](A)=sup_{r>0} C_s(r,A).
This is equality with the unnormalized diameter-power measure in the problem, with no dimensional factor.

If 0<r'≤r, every r'-cover is an r-cover, so C_s(r,A)≤C_s(r',A). Every positive extended r admits a positive finite real δ with ofReal δ≤r (take δ=1 for r=∞ and, for finite r, δ=r.toReal/2). Consequently the supremum is unchanged on restricting to ofReal δ, δ>0:
  μH[s](A)=sup_{δ>0} C_s(ofReal δ,A).
This also proves that zero at every positive finite scale is equivalent to zero measure. If μH[s](A)=0 then each C_s(ofReal δ,A)=0. For any ε>0 this infimum is strictly below ofReal ε. If every admissible cover had cost≥ofReal ε, then ofReal ε would be a lower bound for the infimum, a contradiction. Hence there is an admissible cover with cost<ofReal ε. The successive infima in content have exactly the same meaning as the infimum over the subtype of covers with its two constraints. No topological or measurability property of U_i has been used.

B102: The upper-bound construction, uniform also for zero-dimensional X.
Let X be any metric space, A⊆X, q>0, and assume μH[q](A)=0. We show μH[q+1](A×I)=0 in the maximum metric. Fix an arbitrary target scale δ>0 and error ε>0. Set r=min(1,δ), so 0<r≤1 and r≤δ. By B101 choose a cover U_i of A with ediam U_i≤r/2 and Σ_i(ediam U_i)^q<ε/2. Since the scale bound is finite, write a_i=(ediam U_i).toReal; then 0≤a_i≤r/2 and ediam U_i=ofReal a_i.

Choose positive numerical bounds ρ_i≤r/2 as follows. If a_i>0, put ρ_i=a_i. If a_i=0, put
  ρ_i=(1/2) min(r/2, (ε 2^{−i−2})^{1/q}).
All entries in this minimum are positive. In the zero case ρ_i^q<ε 2^{−i−2}; indeed ρ_i is strictly less than the second entry and the q-th power is strictly increasing on positive reals. For every i we have a_i≤ρ_i, ρ_i>0, ρ_i≤r/2 and
  ρ_i^q≤a_i^q+ε 2^{−i−2}.
The geometric series Σ_{i≥0}2^{−i−2}=1/2 gives Σ_iρ_i^q<ε. To see this without assuming summability in advance, the finite-sum identity for the first m geometric terms is (1/2)(1−2^{−m}); nonnegative infinite sums are the suprema of their finite subsums, yielding the stated value and comparison. There is no need to change a singleton into a positive-diameter set. Empty U_i are allowed and receive the same small positive numerical bound.

For each i let N_i=ceil(1/ρ_i)∈ℕ. Because 0<ρ_i≤1, N_i≥1,
  1/N_i≤ρ_i,  N_i≤1/ρ_i+1≤2/ρ_i.
For j=0,…,N_i−1 put K_{i,j}=[j/N_i,(j+1)/N_i]. These closed intervals cover I: for t<1 choose the integer part of N_i t, and for t=1 choose j=N_i−1. Any two points of K_{i,j} differ by at most 1/N_i, so its diameter is at most ρ_i. The sets U_i×K_{i,j} cover A×I. By the maximum formula and diameter characterization in B009 their diameters are at most ρ_i≤r≤δ. Their (q+1)-cost is at most
  Σ_i N_i ρ_i^{q+1} ≤ 2 Σ_i ρ_i^q < 2ε.
Here ρ_i>0 justifies ρ_i^{q+1}/ρ_i=ρ_i^q. The indexing set {(i,j):i∈ℕ, 0≤j<N_i} is countable, and can be injected into ℕ and padded by empty sets. Reindexing the sum yields exactly the displayed row sums, since each row is finite; equivalently this equality holds by taking suprema over finite subsums. Thus this is an allowed countable cover.

It follows that C_{q+1}(ofReal δ,A×I)≤2ε for every ε>0. This content must be zero: a strictly positive finite lower bound would be contradicted by taking ε below half that bound, and ∞ is contradicted already by ε=1. Since δ was arbitrary, B101 gives μH[q+1](A×I)=0. This proof does not require a nonzero ambient dimension, nonemptiness of A, compactness, or any measurability of A.

B103: Slicing lower bound, including possibly infinite content.
Let X be any metric space, A⊆X, s>0 and δ>0. Put P_A=A×I and c=C_s(ofReal δ,A)∈[0,∞]. Take an arbitrary countable δ-cover V_i of P_A. Put ρ_i=(ediam V_i).toReal, A_i=π_X(V_i), B_i=π_ℝ(V_i). Since ediam V_i≤ofReal δ<∞, its extended diameter equals ofReal ρ_i and 0≤ρ_i≤δ. The maximum distance formula B009 gives ediam A_i≤ofReal ρ_i and ediam B_i≤ofReal ρ_i: for any two projected points choose their respective preimages in V_i, bound their coordinate distance by the product distance, and then by ediam V_i. This argument does not assert any measurability of the projections.

Fix ε>0 and define real
  η_i=ε 2^{−i−1}/(1+ρ_i^s)>0.
For V_i=∅ put J_i=∅. For V_i nonempty, B_i is nonempty and has finite diameter, hence is bounded by B008. Let α_i=sInf B_i and β_i=sSup B_i. Again B008 gives B_i⊆[α_i,β_i] and β_i−α_i≤ρ_i; the last inequality follows from ediam B_i=ofReal(β_i−α_i)≤ofReal ρ_i and β_i−α_i≥0. Let
  J_i=(α_i−η_i/2, β_i+η_i/2).
It contains B_i and is open with length β_i−α_i+η_i≤ρ_i+η_i. In both the empty and nonempty cases J_i is Borel measurable, contains B_i and, by B007 and measure monotonicity,
  volume(J_i∩I)≤ofReal(ρ_i+η_i).
No measurability of B_i itself is needed.

For each t∈I define W_i(t)=A_i when t∈J_i, and ∅ otherwise. This is an admissible δ-cover of A: for x∈A some V_i contains (x,t), which implies x∈A_i and t∈B_i⊆J_i. Its diameter is at most ρ_i in the active case and zero otherwise. B101 and monotonicity of the s-th power on nonnegative numbers therefore give the pointwise extended inequality
  c≤Σ_i ρ_i^s 1_{J_i}(t)  (t∈I).
Only the functions of t on the right will be integrated; their measurable sets are J_i, not the original cover or projections.

Apply B006 with μ=Lebesgue volume on ℝ, w_i=ofReal(ρ_i^s), this I and these J_i. By B007 volume I=1. B006 is valid for any extended c, so it gives
  c≤Σ_i ρ_i^s volume(J_i∩I)
    ≤Σ_i ρ_i^s(ρ_i+η_i)
    =Σ_i ρ_i^{s+1}+Σ_i η_iρ_i^s
    ≤Σ_i ρ_i^{s+1}+ε.
Every displayed term is nonnegative. At ρ_i=0, the product and power identities hold since s>0. The final error bound follows termwise from
  η_iρ_i^s=ε 2^{−i−1} ρ_i^s/(1+ρ_i^s)≤ε 2^{−i−1}
and Σ_i2^{−i−1}=1, whose finite partial sums are 1−2^{−m}. The equality separating the sums and all comparisons are identities/inequalities of nonnegative sums; they do not require an a priori finite cost.

Let S=Σ_iρ_i^{s+1}. If S=∞, c≤S is immediate. If S<∞, the preceding bound at ε=1 forces c<∞. If c>S, choose ε=(c−S)/2 after identifying these finite extended values with real numbers; then c≤S+ε<c, a contradiction. Thus c≤S in all cases. Empty V_i have ρ_i=0 and contribute zero. Since V_i was an arbitrary admissible δ-cover, c is a lower bound for all its costs, so
  C_s(ofReal δ,A)≤C_{s+1}(ofReal δ,A×I).
If there is no admissible cover the right side is ∞ and the inequality is immediate, so this step is valid for every metric space. Taking the supremum over positive real δ in B101 yields
  μH[s](A)≤μH[s+1](A×I).
The construction replaces the original proof's finite-content assertion and its compactness-based proof by an extended-valued inequality. No finiteness or regularity hypothesis has been added or silently used.

B104: Recovering exactly the target from these bounds.
Return to the fixed compact nonempty E⊆X_n. By B004, dimH E≤n<∞, so let D be its nonnegative finite real representative (in Lean, (dimH E).toReal). Then 0≤D≤n and dimH E=ofReal D. No exclusion of n=0 is involved.

For any real q>D, we have q>0. Apply the first critical-exponent implication in B002 with the nonnegative real q: μH[q](E)=0. By B102, μH[q+1](P)=0. The zero-measure converse in B002 gives dimH P≤ofReal(q+1). These bounds for all q>D imply dimH P≤ofReal(D+1). More explicitly the choice q=D+1 first shows dimH P finite; if its real representative were greater than D+1, taking q strictly between D and (dimH P).toReal−1 contradicts the corresponding bound. All constants 2 in B102 are independent of E and the chosen cover; no target parameter range or uniformity has changed.

If D>0, fix any real s with 0<s<D. B002 gives μH[s](E)=∞. By B103, μH[s+1](P)=∞, so the infinite-measure implication in B002 gives dimH P≥ofReal(s+1). These inequalities for every s∈(0,D) imply dimH P≥ofReal(D+1). Indeed if its finite real representative d were <D+1, choose s strictly between max(0,d−1) and D; then s>0 and d<s+1, a contradiction. The representative is finite by the upper bound already proved.

If D=0, choose x₀∈E using the stipulated nonemptiness. The map f:ℝ→X_n×ℝ, f(t)=(x₀,t), is an isometry by B009, since max(0,dist(t,u))=dist(t,u). Its image of I is contained in P. Apply isometry invariance and dimension monotonicity in B003, and B005, to obtain
  1=dimH I=dimH(f(I))≤dimH P.
This is exactly dimH P≥D+1 in this case. For n=0, B004 forces D=0, so this branch proves the lower bound and B102 proves the upper bound without any appeal to positive-dimensional balls.

In either case dimH P=ofReal(D+1)=dimH E+1. The prepared adapter B010 now gives dimH F=dimH P, hence
  dimH(E×[0,1])=dimH E+1
in the required Euclidean ℝ^(n+1), under the explicit coordinate identification j_n. The dimension is finite, so this equality in ℝ≥0∞ is the same equality of real Hausdorff dimensions in the target. Compactness and nonemptiness remain exactly the original assumptions of the final theorem; this proof in fact uses only nonemptiness in addition to the Euclidean ambient domain. It neither changes H nor removes either hypothesis from the requested theorem.

Dependency replacements and scope.
The original ambient cube-counting and separate ℝ^0 argument are replaced by the stronger native ambient estimate B004. The original positive-diameter cover replacement and Euclidean sqrt(2) product-cover calculation are replaced by B101–B102 in the maximum metric, followed by the explicitly prepared Euclidean adapter B010. The original lower-bound integration argument is retained in exact form as B103 using the prepared nonnegative integration theorem B006 and real interval/diameter facts B007–B009; its finiteness-of-content subargument is eliminated by treating c as extended-valued. The original standalone proof that dimH I=1 is replaced by native B005. Critical exponents are provided by B002, and the isometric-slice argument by B003 and B009. Thus every imported substantive analytic ingredient has an actual pinned Lean proof, and all newly introduced covering/slicing arguments are explicit class-3 derivations from them. There are no class-2 library migrations and no residual class-4 assumptions. The assertions in this proof and the machine checks of its prepared native parts still await the single subsequent mathematical Audit A; native compilation is not a claim of mathematical acceptance of this basis proof.
lean_header:
import Mathlib
noncomputable section
open scoped ENNReal NNReal
open Set MeasureTheory MeasureTheory.Measure
namespace YuiGeometry
abbrev Space (n : ℕ) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)
def content {X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] (s : ℝ) (r : ℝ≥0∞) (A : Set X) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨅ (U : ℕ → Set X) (_ : A ⊆ ⋃ i, U i) (_ : ∀ i, Metric.ediam (U i) ≤ r),
    ∑' i, Metric.ediam (U i) ^ s
def join (n : ℕ) (p : Space n × ℝ) : Space (n + 1) :=
  WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.snoc (fun i => p.1 i) p.2)
def cylinder (n : ℕ) (A : Set (Space n)) : Set (Space (n + 1)) :=
  join n '' (A ×ˢ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1)
end YuiGeometry

dependencies.statement: For every metric space X with its Borel measurable structure, every real exponent s and every A⊆X, the (unnormalized) Hausdorff measure μH[s](A) equals sup over r∈[0,∞], r>0, of the infimum over sequences U_i of sets covering A with ediam(U_i)≤r, of Σ_i sup_{h:U_i nonempty} ediam(U_i)^s. Thus empty cover members have cost zero, including at exponent zero.

origin.revision: Pinned Mathlib supplied by read_mathlib and the native basis checker in this stage.

lean.type:
∀ (X : Type*) [MetricSpace X] [MeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X] (s : ℝ) (A : Set X),
  hausdorffMeasure s A =
    ⨆ (r : ℝ≥0∞) (_ : 0 < r),
      ⨅ (U : ℕ → Set X) (_ : A ⊆ ⋃ i, U i) (_ : ∀ i, Metric.ediam (U i) ≤ r),
        ∑' i, ⨆ _ : (U i).Nonempty, Metric.ediam (U i) ^ s
lean.proof:
intro X _ _ _ s A
exact hausdorffMeasure_apply s A

dependencies.justification: This is the exact native covering formula, with no normalization factor or restriction to measurable covering sets. The cost with no Nonempty supremum will be identified only for s>0 in B101.

dependencies.statement: For every metric space X with Borel measure structure, every A⊆X and d≥0 finite (d∈ℝ≥0): dimH(A)<d implies μH[d](A)=0; d<dimH(A) implies μH[d](A)=∞; μH[d](A)=0 implies dimH(A)≤d; and μH[d](A)=∞ implies d≤dimH(A). Dimensions and comparisons are in ℝ≥0∞.

origin.revision: Pinned Mathlib supplied by read_mathlib and the native basis checker in this stage.

lean.type:
∀ (X : Type*) [MetricSpace X] [MeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X] (A : Set X) (d : ℝ≥0),
  (dimH A < (d : ℝ≥0∞) → hausdorffMeasure (d : ℝ) A = 0) ∧
  ((d : ℝ≥0∞) < dimH A → hausdorffMeasure (d : ℝ) A = ⊤) ∧
  (hausdorffMeasure (d : ℝ) A = 0 → dimH A ≤ (d : ℝ≥0∞)) ∧
  (hausdorffMeasure (d : ℝ) A = ⊤ → (d : ℝ≥0∞) ≤ dimH A)
lean.proof:
intro X _ _ _ A d
refine ⟨fun h => hausdorffMeasure_of_dimH_lt h, fun h => hausdorffMeasure_of_lt_dimH h, ?_, fun h => le_dimH_of_hausdorffMeasure_eq_top h⟩
intro h
exact dimH_le_of_hausdorffMeasure_ne_top (by rw [h]; exact ENNReal.zero_ne_top)

dependencies.justification: Only the native characteristic properties are bundled. The third clause follows by replacing zero by a value different from top, using 0≠∞. This proof binds all spaces, instances, sets and exponents.

dependencies.statement: For any metric spaces X,Y, Hausdorff dimension is monotone under inclusion of subsets of X, and every isometry f:X→Y preserves the dimension of every set A⊆X under image.

origin.revision: Pinned Mathlib supplied by read_mathlib and the native basis checker in this stage.

lean.type:
∀ (X Y : Type*) [MetricSpace X] [MetricSpace Y],
  (∀ (A B : Set X), A ⊆ B → dimH A ≤ dimH B) ∧
  (∀ (f : X → Y), Isometry f → ∀ (A : Set X), dimH (f '' A) = dimH A)
lean.proof:
intro X Y _ _
exact ⟨fun A B h => dimH_mono h, fun f h A => h.dimH_image A⟩

dependencies.justification: The isometry assertion needs no surjectivity and can be used for t↦(x₀,t). The dimension convention for the empty set remains Mathlib's zero.

dependencies.statement: For every n∈ℕ, including n=0, and every A⊆EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), dimH(A)≤n (as an extended nonnegative real). In particular its dimension is finite and has a nonnegative real representative.

origin.revision: Pinned Mathlib supplied by read_mathlib and the native basis checker in this stage.

lean.type: ∀ (n : ℕ) (A : Set (YuiGeometry.Space n)), dimH A ≤ (n : ℝ≥0∞)
lean.proof:
intro n A
calc
  dimH A ≤ dimH (Set.univ : Set (YuiGeometry.Space n)) := dimH_mono (Set.subset_univ A)
  _ = (n : ℝ≥0∞) := by rw [Real.dimH_univ_eq_finrank]; simp [YuiGeometry.Space]

dependencies.justification: The native finite-dimensional ambient-dimension formula replaces the original cube counting proof. Compactness is not needed for this stronger bound. There is no exclusion of the zero vector space.

dependencies.statement: The Hausdorff dimension of the closed real interval [0,1], with its ordinary distance, is one.

origin.revision: Pinned Mathlib supplied by read_mathlib and the native basis checker in this stage.

lean.proof:
simpa only [segment_eq_Icc (show (0 : ℝ) ≤ 1 by norm_num)] using
  (Real.dimH_segment (E := ℝ) (x := 0) (y := 1) (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) ≠ 1))

dependencies.justification: This uses the native dimension theorem for a nondegenerate segment, specialized to the actual unit interval. It replaces both length-cover critical-exponent arguments in the original proof.

dependencies.statement: For every measurable space X, measure μ, measurable I⊆X, sequence of measurable sets J_i⊆X, weights w_i∈ℝ≥0∞, and c∈ℝ≥0∞: if c≤Σ_i 1_{J_i}(t)w_i for every t∈I, then c μ(I)≤Σ_i w_i μ(J_i∩I). Infinite c and divergent series are permitted.

origin.revision: Pinned Mathlib supplied by read_mathlib and the native basis checker in this stage.

lean.type:
∀ (X : Type*) [MeasurableSpace X] (μ : Measure X) (I : Set X) (J : ℕ → Set X)
  (w : ℕ → ℝ≥0∞) (c : ℝ≥0∞),
  MeasurableSet I → (∀ i, MeasurableSet (J i)) →
  (∀ t ∈ I, c ≤ ∑' i, (J i).indicator (fun _ => w i) t) →
  c * μ I ≤ ∑' i, w i * μ (J i ∩ I)
lean.proof:
intro X _ μ I J w c hI hJ h
classical
calc
  c * μ I = ∫⁻ t, I.indicator (fun _ => c) t ∂μ :=
    (lintegral_indicator_const hI c).symm
  _ ≤ ∫⁻ t, ∑' i, (J i ∩ I).indicator (fun _ => w i) t ∂μ := by
    apply lintegral_mono
    intro t
    by_cases ht : t ∈ I
    · simpa only [Set.indicator_apply, Set.mem_inter_iff, ht, and_true, if_true] using h t ht
    · simp [Set.indicator_apply, ht]
  _ = ∑' i, ∫⁻ t, (J i ∩ I).indicator (fun _ => w i) t ∂μ :=
    lintegral_tsum (fun i => (measurable_const.indicator ((hJ i).inter hI)).aemeasurable)
  _ = ∑' i, w i * μ (J i ∩ I) := by
    congr 1
    funext i
    exact lintegral_indicator_const ((hJ i).inter hI) (w i)

dependencies.justification: A concrete compatibility adapter derived from nonnegative Tonelli and indicator integration. The pointwise comparison is applied after multiplying by 1_I; no measurability of the arbitrary cover sets or projections is introduced. No finiteness of c is required.

dependencies.statement: For every real a,b, Lebesgue volume of [a,b] and of (a,b) is ENNReal.ofReal(b−a), including empty or degenerate intervals.

origin.revision: Pinned Mathlib supplied by read_mathlib and the native basis checker in this stage.

lean.type:
∀ (a b : ℝ),
  volume (Set.Icc a b) = ENNReal.ofReal (b - a) ∧
  volume (Set.Ioo a b) = ENNReal.ofReal (b - a)

dependencies.justification: In particular volume([0,1])=1. Monotonicity then bounds volume(J∩[0,1]) by the length of an open interval J. Native measure monotonicity is freely available.

dependencies.statement: For every metric space X and set A⊆X, A is bounded iff ediam(A)≠∞. For every bounded real set B, ediam(B)=ofReal(sSup B−sInf B), and every x∈B satisfies sInf B≤x≤sSup B.

origin.revision: Pinned Mathlib supplied by read_mathlib and the native basis checker in this stage.

lean.type:
(∀ (X : Type*) [MetricSpace X] (A : Set X),
  Bornology.IsBounded A ↔ Metric.ediam A ≠ ⊤) ∧
 (∀ (B : Set ℝ), Bornology.IsBounded B →
  Metric.ediam B = ENNReal.ofReal (sSup B - sInf B) ∧
  ∀ x ∈ B, sInf B ≤ x ∧ x ≤ sSup B)
lean.proof:
constructor
· intro X _ A
  exact Metric.isBounded_iff_ediam_ne_top
· intro B hB
  exact ⟨Real.ediam_eq hB, fun x hx => hB.subset_Icc_sInf_sSup hx⟩

dependencies.justification: Provides the exact bounded-set diameter and endpoint facts needed to enclose real projections in open intervals. Supremum and infimum require no measurability of B.

dependencies.statement: For metric spaces X,Y the standard product distance is the maximum of the two coordinate extended distances. For A⊆X and r∈ℝ≥0∞, ediam(A)≤r iff every pair x,y∈A has edist(x,y)≤r.

origin.revision: Pinned Mathlib supplied by read_mathlib and the native basis checker in this stage.

lean.type:
∀ (X Y : Type*) [MetricSpace X] [MetricSpace Y],
  (∀ p q : X × Y, edist p q = max (edist p.1 q.1) (edist p.2 q.2)) ∧
  (∀ (A : Set X) (r : ℝ≥0∞),
    Metric.ediam A ≤ r ↔ ∀ x ∈ A, ∀ y ∈ A, edist x y ≤ r)
lean.proof:
intro X Y _ _
exact ⟨fun p q => Prod.edist_eq p q, fun A r => Metric.ediam_le_iff⟩

dependencies.justification: These native identities justify both coordinate projection diameter bounds and the bound ediam(U×K)≤r whenever both factors have diameter≤r. They also show t↦(x₀,t) is an isometry.

dependencies.statement: For every n∈ℕ and A⊆EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), the coordinate concatenation join_n(x,t)=(x₀,…,x_{n−1},t) preserves Hausdorff dimension under image of A×[0,1]: dimH(cylinder_n A)=dimH(A×[0,1]), where the right-hand product uses the maximum metric and the left uses the Euclidean metric on ℝ^(n+1).

origin.revision: Pinned Mathlib supplied by read_mathlib and the native basis checker in this stage.

lean.type:
∀ (n : ℕ) (A : Set (YuiGeometry.Space n)),
  dimH (YuiGeometry.cylinder n A) = dimH (A ×ˢ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1)
lean.proof:
intro n A
let e : (YuiGeometry.Space n × ℝ) ≃ₗ[ℝ] YuiGeometry.Space (n + 1) :=
  { toFun := YuiGeometry.join n
    invFun := fun z => (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i : Fin n => z i.castSucc), z (Fin.last n))
    left_inv := by
      intro p

    right_inv := by
      intro z
      ext i
      refine Fin.lastCases ?_ (fun j => ?_) i
      · simp [YuiGeometry.join]
      · simp [YuiGeometry.join]
    map_add' := by
      intro p q
      ext i
      refine Fin.lastCases ?_ (fun j => ?_) i <;> simp [YuiGeometry.join]

      intro c p

dependencies.justification: The coordinate concatenation is explicitly a real linear equivalence, with inverse given by the first n coordinates and the last coordinate. Finite dimensionality makes it a continuous linear equivalence, so both it and its inverse are Lipschitz. The prepared proof supplies the metric-change adapter now. This also works for n=0; no arbitrary unnamed finite-dimensional isomorphism changes the set.

dependencies.statement: For every metric space X, A⊆X and real s>0, define C_s(r,A) as in YuiGeometry.content, using countable covers, extended diameters and cost Σ ediam(U_i)^s. With the Borel structure on X, μH[s](A)=sup_{r>0} C_s(r,A)=sup_{δ∈ℝ,δ>0} C_s(ofReal δ,A). Every eligible cover bounds C_s from above by its cost. If μH[s](A)=0, then at every positive finite scale δ and for every ε>0 there is such a cover with cost<ofReal ε.
